reason: Fresh post-#387 audit proves that Element is intended to be the sole Product renderer while legacy frontend remains independently reachable through backend static serving and catch-all HTML fallback, is still copied by WP1/WP6/WP7 production-style payload authorities, and is still treated by executable root-cause governance as current Product truth. Consumer analysis also proves that legitimate notification sounds and generated Yance brand assets are incorrectly hosted beneath the legacy frontend authority. This authorization retires the duplicate Product surface across HTTP reachability, production payload construction and executable governance in one root-cause work package, while re-homing legitimate supporting assets under canonical non-legacy authorities. User selected a lively classic default sound direction; official built-in sound bytes must come from the pinned CC0 Kenney Interface Sounds source rather than legacy QQ/WeChat/Samsung-labelled assets whose redistribution provenance is not established. No redirect, feature flag, hidden fallback, packaging-only exclusion, test weakening or second authority is permitted.

digestCanonicalization.pathNormalization: Require exact repository-relative normalized paths, remove duplicates, then sort with JavaScript default Array.prototype.sort().
digestCanonicalization.canonicalText: Join the normalized sorted unique path list with LF and append exactly one trailing LF before hashing.

expectedFailures: backend/server.js still serves frontend as a static root and returns frontend/index.html for arbitrary non-API GET paths.
WP1/WP6/WP7 still identify or copy frontend as a runtime/production root rather than excluding the duplicate Product renderer.
branding build/verify still materializes and validates duplicate runtime branding below frontend instead of binding canonical assets/branding/yance directly.
notification sound runtime still resolves built-in files below frontend/assets/sounds and the active built-in catalog still admits legacy imported branded patterns.
root-cause executable governance still treats legacy frontend readers/assets as current Product authority.

requiredBehavior: Remove backend static serving of the legacy frontend tree and remove the catch-all frontend/index.html fallback; non-API paths must not return legacy Product HTML.
Keep backend API/control-plane routes and structured error handling intact.
Make Element the only Product renderer in packaged/runtime authority.
Remove frontend from WP1 runtime payload allowlist, WP6 production roots and WP7 reviewed Product roots; add the canonical assets root only where legitimate canonical brand assets are required.
Update source-closure verification so a packaged Product containing a second launchable legacy frontend is rejected rather than required.
Retire legacy frontend readers/assets from executable root-cause governance while preserving truthful historical audit classification.
Keep the source frontend tree available as historical material in this work package; source deletion is not evidence of runtime retirement and is not required.
forbiddenBehavior: Do not replace legacy HTML fallback with a redirect, feature flag, secret route, alternate static mount or other hidden second renderer.
Do not keep frontend in production payload only to satisfy old tests.
Do not weaken Product Final, source-closure, brand, native or architecture verification.
Do not delete legitimate supporting assets before their canonical consumer path is migrated.

requiredBehavior: Make assets/branding/yance the single generated and verified Yance brand asset authority.
Stop branding build scripts from recreating runtime copies under frontend.
Bind payload verification and WP1 branding tests to canonical packaged assets instead of frontend copies.
Preserve deterministic generated PNG/ICO/SVG identity checks against the canonical brand manifest.
